answers.answer: I CAN produce the labelled placeholder illustration, and it already lives in my grounded KB2 node OWN_KNITTING_BREAKEVEN. Formula (untagged identity): breakeven_utilisation = owned_fixed_period_cost / ((jobwork_unit_rate - owned_variable_unit_cost) * period_capacity). Worked stand-in [ESTIMATE: arithmetic, LOW-MED, placeholder inputs because the rate is [UNKNOWN]]: owned_fixed_period_cost ~$7,500/mo (amortised landed machine + programmer seat + skilled payroll + power); conversion SAVING band (jobwork_unit_rate minus owned_variable_unit_cost) ~$5/sweater; period_capacity ~800 sweaters/mo (linker-bound). breakeven = 7500 / (5*800) = 7500/4000 = 1.875 -> ABOVE 1.0, so subcontract wins at launch (utilisation starved: you cannot run a line at 187.5% utilisation). Crucially, the input I pick is the SAVING (jobwork_rate - owned_variable_cost), NOT the [UNKNOWN] jobwork_rate itself; the illustration holds for ANY jobwork_rate whose saving-over-owned-variable-cost is ~$5. To answer the smuggling trap honestly: yes, a $5 saving DOES encode an implied minimum jobwork rate = $5 + owned_variable_unit_cost. But I hold owned_variable_unit_cost [UNKNOWN] too, so I am not asserting a specific Rs/piece rate; I am asserting a SAVING band and showing the breakeven is >1.0 across it. If the true saving were as high as ~$9.4/sweater, breakeven would fall to 7500/(9.4*800)=~1.0 -- so the honest boundary is: subcontract wins at launch UNLESS the per-sweater conversion saving over the owned line exceeds ~$9-10 AND the linker-bound line is genuinely filled, neither of which holds at capsule volume. This is a computed conclusion from labelled stand-ins, not a bare assertion, and it does not quote the [UNKNOWN] rate.

answers.answer: The linking-last / linker-is-bottleneck verdict SURVIVES on a mechanism independent of the transferred ~60% ratio, so it does not inherit the ratio's LOW-MED softness for SEQUENCING. My KB2 node LINKING_LAST grounds own-linking-last on THREE ratio-free arguments: (1) the linker sets the daily THROUGHPUT ceiling in absolute pc/shift terms (~20-45 sweaters/linker/shift, the linker not the knitting machine caps output) -- a capacity fact, not a cost-ratio; (2) the skilled linker is the HARDEST role to re-hire after the lean season -- a labour-scarcity/staffing fact; (3) linking is the QC-critical signature seam, so it is simultaneously the highest-value and most operationally-dangerous step to own -- a quality/risk fact. None of these depends on the ~60% link:knit cost ratio being scale-free. The ~60% ratio (FF-costing study: knitting ~$0.74/pc, linking ~$0.45/pc) is used ONLY as SHAPE for the COST-band bounding, explicitly [DOWNGRADED] to LOW-MED and flagged as productivity/wage-dependent (Ludhiana labour is cheaper, pc/operator-day [UNKNOWN]). You are right that the ratio itself is not scale-free -- if Ludhiana's knit-vs-link productivity gap differed, the 60% could move. But the SEQUENCING verdict (linking last, knitting before it) rests on throughput-ceiling + hardest-re-hire + QC-criticality, which are the scarcity/skill mechanisms you name, not on the ratio. So I do NOT concede that 'linking last' inherits the ratio's softness: I concede the ratio is not scale-free for the COST shape (already flagged [DOWNGRADED]), and I affirm the sequencing survives independently.

answers.answer: Calling A2 'the floor' bare is scope-honest but MISLEADING unless a caveat travels with it, and I am entitled to say only the ex-factory half. WHAT I AM ENTITLED TO SAY: 'A2 fine-acrylic is the cheapest article at the FACTORY GATE (~$3.5-8 ex-factory, the floor of my three bands).' That is a pure ex-factory statement, true within my lane. WHAT I MAY NOT SAY: that A2 is the cheapest article to SELL or land, because the ~32% acrylic/MMF US duty (6110.30.30, ~2x cotton's ~16.5%) is T9's, not mine, and it erases A2's factory-gate lead at the border -- I must not let that ~32% leak INTO my band, but I also must not present the floor as if it survives the hand-off. SMALLEST HONEST CAVEAT that must travel with 'A2 is the floor': 'A2 is the ex-factory floor ONLY; its advantage does not survive the hand-off -- acrylic/MMF carries the ~32% US duty outlier (T9) and the inverted-duty/GST refund drag that bites A2 specifically on the India cash-cycle side (magnitude [UNKNOWN]). Whether A2 remains cheapest LANDED is unit_economics' call, not mine.' So: 'A2 is the floor' + '...ex-factory only; the lead evaporates at the border and in the refund lag; landed ranking is T9's' is the minimum honest statement. Naming it bare would hand T9 a number that reads as an acrylic-wins recommendation I am not entitled to make.

answers.answer: The bright-line is UTILISATION INTENT and OUTPUT DESTINATION, not the machine class -- and yes, this needs to be stated explicitly because a used linker in the sampling cell IS the same machine class as the linking bottleneck. My spec/KB2 draw the line as: the iteration cell owns a used linker to LINK PROTOTYPES/SAMPLES ONLY (overnight iteration of proven-vs-unproven designs), on a SPEED/CONTROL axis, and sends ONLY PROVEN DESIGNS to the mesh/FOB for BULK linking (KB2 glossary 'own the iteration loop': 'iterate prototypes in-house... then send only proven designs to the mesh/FOB for bulk... the utilisation argument against owning bulk does not apply'; conflicts_and_dominance[5]: 'NOT owning bulk knitting'). The moment that cell's linker starts linking SALEABLE BULK units, it stops being iteration and becomes in-sourced bulk linking -- which is forbidden until LINKING_LAST's falsifiable conditions hold (after knitting, lean-season-staffable linkers, the utilisation breakeven cleared). BRIGHT-LINE (the honest formulation): an iteration-cell linker may link only sample/PPS/fit pieces and pre-production protos, never units that enter the saleable order; if a proto run is scaled into sellable inventory, it has crossed into bulk and must go to the mesh/FOB or clear the LINKING_LAST gate. AUTHORITY: linker CAPACITY and the machine layer are knit_machine_strategist's lane (router dominance) and build=NEVER stands; owning a sub-$4k USED linker for sampling is not building a machine and not owning bulk capacity, so it does not breach build-NEVER -- but it DOES risk breaching linking-last if the destination line blurs. HONEST DEFECT: my spec asserts the speed-axis carve-out and says 'this is NOT owning bulk knitting', but it does NOT author the explicit sample-only / no-saleable-units bright-line, so the equipment list (used linker ~$500-4,000) could be read as authorising owning the scarce linker early through the sampling-cell door.

answers.answer: The two calendars genuinely do not align, and I can name the squeeze but NOT size the demand half -- that is T7/T9's lane, and I must not over-claim a launch date. SUPPLY side (mine): avoid committing a launch drop into the Ludhiana Jul-Oct winter-hosiery PEAK, when the cluster's own winter orders stretch job-work lead time and working capital exactly when a tiny buyer has least queue priority (KB3 SEASONAL_CASH_TIMING + WORKING_CAPITAL_TRAP; my capabilities[4]). Conversion is ~6-12 weeks yarn-in to goods-ready (KB3), then ocean India->US adds weeks (T9). DEMAND side (NOT mine): California/Turlock is WARM, so heavy knitwear sells fewer months (SCOPE_GLOSSARY: warm-California climate inverts the winter-woollen instinct) and the DECISION_MEMO leads A3-hero into that short cool-season window. THE SQUEEZE: to avoid the Jul-Oct supply peak yet arrive for the short California cool season after ~6-12 wks conversion + weeks of ocean, the order must be placed on a calendar that dodges the Ludhiana peak AND lands stock before the cool window -- these can conflict, and I CANNOT prove the calendar closes because the demand-window timing and the sell-through curve are T7/T9's. HONEST CONCESSION: 'avoid Jul-Oct' + ocean lead + a warm-market demand window is a scheduling squeeze I NAME (as a working-capital-trap amplifier) but CANNOT SIZE; the demand-arrival half (when California actually buys sweaters, and how long the window is) belongs to brand_market (T7) and the landed lead-time model to unit_economics (T9). I stay on the supply/cash-cycle side and defer the demand-timing half rather than assert a launch date.

answers.answer: I can cleanly separate the RATE-INDEPENDENT decisions (survive any quote outcome) from the ones PARKED behind the [UNKNOWN]s -- I am delivering real decisions, not deferring the whole segment. RATE-INDEPENDENT VERDICTS (a quote run cannot overturn these): (1) NEVER own a dyehouse at any volume -- grounded on crore-scale CETP/NGT closure risk (KB2 NEVER_OWN_DYEHOUSE), not on any rate; (2) NEVER build a knitting machine -- ~$2M-10M+ vs sub-$20k used (KB2 NEVER_BUILD_MACHINE), rate-independent; (3) dye-lot MOQ (~150-500 kg/colour), NOT garment MOQ, is the binding minimum, forcing a colour-starved 2-4-colour launch (KB3 DYE_LOT_MOQ) -- structural, holds at any knit+LINK rate; (4) the launch is sized by the FIRST CHEQUE (dye MOQ + setup + months of tied cash), not unit-cost x pieces; the working-capital trap, not the unit cost, is the launch killer (KB3 WORKING_CAPITAL_TRAP) -- rate-independent; (5) true micro cost sits ~1.3-2x the band midpoint (setup + small-batch surcharge), so the bands are a FLOOR -- holds at any rate; (6) OWN design + brand + US import always; buy/subcontract everything upstream; graduate to owning a step only on proven sustained single-program volume, LINKING LAST -- the ordering is rate-independent even though the crossover volume is not; (7) ex-factory is the least-decisive part -- contribution-margin-after-CAC (T7/T9), not factory cost, decides viability.
